#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from LSF

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# LSF resources:
#   -nnodes 1
#   -W 720
#   -J mirge_Y0
#   -q pbatch
#   -G uiuc
#   -o runOutput.%J
#   -e runError.%J

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=12h
#flux: --job-name=mirge_Y0

# Omitted LSF option: -q pbatch (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted LSF option: -G uiuc (account/group)
# Flux accounting/group selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted LSF options: -o/-e with %J token
# LSF's %J token expansion is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Omitted jsrun resource mapping (-g 1, etc.)
# Flux GPU requests and CPU/GPU binding are site/config dependent; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU or with suboptimal binding, causing failure or reduced performance.

module load gcc/7.3.1
module load spectrum-mpi

conda deactivate
conda activate mirgeDriver.Y1nozzle

export PYOPENCL_CTX="port:tesla"
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="/tmp/$USER/xdg-scratch"

# Replace jsrun with flux-run; launch single rank.
flux run -n 1 js_task_info
flux run -n 1 python -u -m mpi4py ./nozzle.py

reasons: The original job required a GPU (jsrun used `-g 1`), but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original job specified a queue (`-q pbatch`) and group/account (`-G uiuc`), but the Flux resource section has no queue/account selection; on sites where these control eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
